name: Calyx Passionfruit-Miso Fizz
description: An unlicensed street-brand soda produced in small batches in the Tier 2-3 boundary districts, combining real passionfruit with a shiro miso brine reduction for a savory-sweet effervescent drink that shouldn't work as well as it does. Distributed through informal networks and select independent shops.
flavor_profile: Tart passionfruit brightness, subtle savory miso salinity, slight fermented depth, lively carbonation
cultural_context: Calyx has become a minor status item in GLMZ's independent food culture — owning a Calyx means you know someone, or know where to look. It's not expensive enough to be a Tier 4 luxury, but the sourcing and distribution model gives it an authenticity cachet that corporate brands can't replicate. Chefs and food-curious Tier 3 professionals seek it out specifically because it's unlicensed.
story_hooks: A corponation's acquisition team has tracked Calyx to its production location and is preparing a buyout offer — the founder has to decide whether to sell out, go further underground, or do something riskier.

The real passionfruit in Calyx comes from a single vertical farm in the Tier 1 border zone — when that farm is threatened by a rezoning order, Calyx's supply chain collapses and the founder needs help.
A food safety inspector is being pressured to shut down Calyx by a competing licensed beverage company — the inspector isn't sure if the product is actually unsafe or if she's being used.
